case.claim: handleAdd's empty-input guard uses multiEmailValue.length === 0, but the state is initialized to [""] and MultiEmail feeds it, so a single blank input passes the length check and reaches the zod array parse instead of being silently returned.
case.trigger: User opens dialog, types nothing (value stays [""]), clicks Add.
case.impact: Instead of an early return, validation fails on the invalid empty string and isInvalidEmail flips the 'emails must be unique/valid' error; mutation is not sent, so behavior depends on whether MultiEmail ever emits [] or strips "".

args.reason: The guard contract is the PR's own early-return for "no emails entered", but its length===0 predicate can never be satisfied in this dialog: state is initialized to [""] (obs_3:e3, obs_4:e1) and MultiEmail's setValue path preserves array length instead of dropping empty entries (obs_9:e4). So the single blank input [""] passes the guard and reaches z.array(z.string().email()).safeParse, which rejects "" and flips isInvalidEmail, surfacing a validation error for an action where no guest was entered. The refutation condition (MultiEmail normalizing empty input to [] or filtering "") is contradicted by the actual onChange handler shown in obs_9:e4; the remaining unread tail only adds more rows, it cannot turn [""] into []. Expected vs actual are established for the same witness (open dialog, type nothing, click Add).
args.expected: With no email entered (state still [\"\"]), clicking Add should hit the empty-input guard and return silently with no validation error and no mutation.
args.actual: [\"\"] has length 1, so the guard is skipped; ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse([\"\"]) fails on z.string().email(), setIsInvalidEmail(true) shows the invalid/unique-emails error even though the user typed nothing.

note: Transport failure regression only; no semantic truth or quality label.
